problem: Find the unit tangent vector to the curve $r(t)=⟨{e}^{-t}\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,{e}^{-t}\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,{e}^{-t}⟩$ at the point where $t=0.$
worked_solution:
For a curve $r(t)=⟨x(t),y(t),z(t)⟩$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t),z(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

First, we find ${r}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{-t}\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{-t}\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{-t})⟩ \\  & =⟨-{e}^{-t}\operatorname{sin}⁡t+{e}^{-t}\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-{e}^{-t}\operatorname{cos}⁡t-{e}^{-t}\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,-{e}^{-t}⟩ \\ {r}^{′}(0) & =⟨-{e}^{-(0)}\operatorname{sin}⁡(0)+{e}^{-(0)}\operatorname{cos}⁡(0),\,-{e}^{-(0)}\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)-{e}^{-(0)}\operatorname{sin}⁡(0),\,-{e}^{-(0)}⟩ \\  & =⟨-0+1,\,-1-0,\,-1⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,-1,\,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(0):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(0)‖ & =\sqrt{(1)^{2}+(-1)^{2}+(-1)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(0)$ and obtain the unit tangent vector to the given curve at the point where $t=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(0) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(0)}{‖{r}^{′}(0)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}⟨1,\,-1,\,-1⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3},\,-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3},\,-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}⟩\end{aligned}
$$
